topics.label: Introduction to cancer mechanisms and hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the lecture's learning outcomes and introduces the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and growth factor independence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematologic and solid tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired differentiation contributes to malignancy using leukemia and intestinal crypt models.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how mutations in p53 and dysregulation of BCL-2 family proteins prevent cancer cells from undergoing programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and bypass the p53-mediated senescence barrier to achieve indefinite replication.

topics.label: Deregulating cellular metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and produce oncometabolites that alter gene expression.

topics.label: Inducing tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the necessity, progression, and molecular balance of new blood vessel formation in supporting tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and detection of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the biological barriers, circulatory dissemination, and genomic features associated with tumor spread to distant tissues.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes, discussing recent hallmark literature, and inviting student questions.
